text: Every table uses variant V1 and the civilian agencies: every awarding agency except Defense (097).

The yearly series is each year's share of civilian dollars in segments with HHI above 2,500 (civilian_by_year.csv). Tests: Kendall's tau between year and share; the least-squares slope in points per year; and the mean of the last 6 years minus the mean of the first 6. Each p-value is one-sided (a rise) and comes from 20,000 shuffles of the 18 yearly values, seed 20261105. Shuffling assumes years are exchangeable, which neighbouring years with shared multi-year awards are not, so the p-values are too small if anything. The same tests run on the series with Veterans Affairs left out, and on the share of segments (unweighted) above 2,500.

A line is one civilian agency and one product code over FY2008 to FY2025, kept when it has at least 6 scored years and at least $10,000,000 in net over them (product codes carry across the code changes for 88.5% of dollars, psc_era_patterns.csv). Gain: the mean HHI of its last 3 scored years minus the mean of its first 3.

For each cutoff, the share of lines whose gain is at least the cutoff, observed and after shuffling each line's own years (500 times). The ratio shuffled over observed estimates the share of flagged lines that chance alone would flag.

Each line's own permutation p-value: the share of its 500 shuffles with a gain at least the observed one. A line is a tested riser when its gain is at least 500 points and its p-value passes the Benjamini-Hochberg rule at q = 0.1 across all kept lines.
